items.q: Is there a student discount at Berlin museums?
items.a: **Yes. At the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin the general reduction is 50 percent**, and students of any age qualify with a valid student card or enrolment certificate. That turns a 14 euro ticket at the Neues Museum, Altes Museum, Bode-Museum or Gemäldegalerie into 7 euros. **The proof has to be with you**, and a student card with no validity dates printed on it is often refused.

items.q: Who gets reduced entry at Berlin's state museums?
items.a: The published list is short: **students, apprentices and trainees, school pupils aged 18 or over, people doing a recognised voluntary service year, jobseekers receiving ALG I, and severely disabled visitors with a degree of disability of 50 or more.** Every one of them needs to show the matching document at the entrance without being asked.

items.q: Are children free at Berlin museums?
items.a: **Anyone under 18 gets in free at the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, not half price.** That covers the Museum Island houses, the Gemäldegalerie and the Hamburger Bahnhof. The Berlinische Galerie is free under 18 too. **Free still means collecting a zero-euro ticket at the desk** or booking it online, then showing ID with a date of birth at the entrance.

items.q: Is there a senior discount at Berlin museums?
items.a: **No. There is no pensioner or senior rate on the state museums' reduction list.** A 70 year old and a 40 year old both pay the full 14 euros at the Neues Museum. Visitors from countries where a senior rate is standard are regularly caught out by this, so budget for full price and use Berlin's large stock of free sights instead.

items.q: Does a Berlin museum pass cover special exhibitions?
items.a: **Usually not.** The 24 euro Museumsinsel-Ticket and the 32 euro three-day Museumspass Berlin cover permanent exhibitions and let you walk straight in, and both are halved to 12 and 16 with proof. Big temporary shows are priced separately: **until 27 September 2026 the Alte Nationalgalerie charges pass holders a surcharge of 6 euros, or 3 reduced**, for its Paul Cassirer exhibition.

items.q: Is there still a free museum Sunday in Berlin?
items.a: **No. Museumssonntag, the free first Sunday of the month, ended in December 2024 and has not returned**, even though plenty of travel pages still promise it. The closest current equivalent is the Berlinische Galerie, where **the first Wednesday of every month costs 7 euros for everyone** with no card or proof needed.
